scenario: AITA for not inviting my boyfriend along when I hang out with my friends | This has been an ongoing argument between my boyfriend (M26) and I (F26) so we're bringing it to the internet to decide whether I'm being an asshole. He's read over what I'm writing and we're both going to accept the decision of internet strangers. For the record we live together. I have always believed that when I'm hanging out with friends I should make an effort to sometimes go alone. This refers both to when I'm hanging out one on one with a friend and when it's a small group of us (like 3-4 friends from high school). When it's a larger group I always invite him. My reasoning for this is: 1. Just because they want to hang out with me doesn't necessarily mean that they want to hang out with my boyfriend at that time (for the record they like him). I feel like there are things that they maybe wouldn't feel comfortable sharing if he was there. 2. Sometimes I feel like by bringing him I'm "rubbing in their face" or reminding them that they aren't in a relationship, and I know that some of them are actively looking. Also I remember how it felt when I was in their place and even though I was happy for them that they were happy I was also a little bit jealous and felt left out. 3. I think that a lot of times people get into relationships and lose touch with their friends. I remember how much it bothered me when I felt like I was losing my friend to a relationship or when they would invite me out but I felt like a 3rd wheel. It's important to me to keep making an effort in my friendships and not give my friends the feeling that they're "in addition to my boyfriend". 4. I feel like sometimes inviting my boyfriend changes the vibe of hanging out, and while that's totally fine, sometimes I feel like my friends want to just hang out "the high school friends" or "just girls". I feel like I also sometimes want this specific vibe. I remember how much it bothered me when I thought that I was hanging out with a friend and I showed up to see that her boyfriend had come along too, even if I liked him I was a little bit sad that we wouldn't have our own time together. Overall I love my boyfriend and things are great when he comes along, but I feel that it's important for me to sometimes prioritize just friend things. This came up again today because I mentioned that I was going to meet with a friend tomorrow and my boyfriend got pissed that I'm not inviting him yet again, and he thinks that I'm taking my friends into account more than him. AITA by not inviting him along? ​ TLDR boyfriend is offended that I want to hang out with a friend without inviting him, AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being an asshole by not inviting my boyfriend when I hang out with my friends. Let me start by understanding the situation better. We've been together for a while, and I really love him. But I also value my friendships, and I think it's important to maintain those connections. Sometimes, when I'm hanging out with just one friend or a small group, I don't invite him. I do invite him when it's a larger group, though. Why do I do this? Well, first, I think that just because my friends want to hang out with me doesn't mean they necessarily want to hang out with my boyfriend at the same time. They like him, but maybe they want to talk about things that are more personal or specific to our friendship. I feel like there are some conversations that are better had without him being there. Second, I don't want to make my friends feel like they're being reminded that they're not in a relationship. Some of them are actively looking for relationships, and I remember how it felt when I was in their shoes. It's a bit sad to always be reminded that you're not in a relationship when your friends are. Third, I think that when people get into relationships, they sometimes lose touch with their friends. I don't want that to happen to me. I want to keep my friendships strong, and I don't want my friends to feel like they're just an addition to my relationship. I want them to feel valued for who they are, not just because they're my friend. Fourth, sometimes inviting my boyfriend changes the vibe of the hangout. While that's totally fine, I also think that my friends might want to hang out with just the "high school friends" or "just girls." I want to respect that and give them that space. I remember feeling sad when I thought that a friend was bringing their boyfriend along, even if I liked him. I wanted our own time together. Overall, I love my boyfriend, and things are great when he comes along. But I feel that it's important for me to sometimes prioritize just friend things. That's why I don't always invite him when I'm hanging out with my friends. Now, my boyfriend is upset because I mentioned I was going to meet with a friend tomorrow and didn't invite him again. He thinks I'm taking my friends into account more than him. Is he right? Am I being an asshole by not inviting him along? I need to think about this carefully. On one hand, I value my friendships and want to maintain them. On the other hand, I don't want my boyfriend to feel left out or unimportant. Maybe there's a way to balance both. Perhaps I can communicate my feelings to him and understand his perspective as well. It's important to have open conversations about this to find a middle ground where both of our needs are respected. I also wonder if there's a way to involve him in some of these hangouts without making it feel forced. Maybe sometimes he can join, and other times, it's just me and my friends. That way, everyone feels respected and valued. It's all about finding that balance. In the end, I think it's important to respect both my need for friendships and my boyfriend's feelings. By communicating openly and finding a compromise, we can both feel satisfied and valued in our relationship.
